q: מטופל בן 75 מתחיל תרופה לשינה העלולה לפגוע בערנות ונוהג בבוקר. איזה מרכיב נדרש בייעוץ לפי חוזר משרד הבריאות על נהיגה?
o: קביעת ההמלצה לפי תחושת הערנות שהמטופל מדווח עליה
הסבר על הסיכון לנהיגה ותיעודו ברשומה הרפואית
מסירת האזהרה בביקורת אם ידווח על קושי בנהיגה
מסירת האזהרה למשפחה כדי שתדריך את המטופל במקומה
explanation:
**ייעוץ על נהיגה** כולל אזהרה מפני השפעת תרופות על הערנות ועל כושר הנהיגה. החוזר דורש גם לתעד את ההסברים והחשש ברשומה; הוא אינו קובע כאן זמן המתנה אחיד לאחר זולפידם (עמ׳ 3, סעיפים 7.2 עד 7.3).
"יש להזהיר את החולה בדבר תופעות לוואי של תרופות העלולות להשפיע על כושר הנהיגה והערנות." (עמ׳ 3).

**א. קביעת ההמלצה לפי תחושת הערנות שהמטופל מדווח עליה.** שגויה, החובה להזהיר על השפעת התרופה אינה מוחלפת בתחושת ערנות סובייקטיבית; זהו יישום של הוראת החוזר (עמ׳ 3).
**ב. הסבר על הסיכון לנהיגה ותיעודו ברשומה הרפואית.** נכונה, זו הוראת החוזר: להזהיר את החולה ולתעד את ההסבר והחשש (עמ׳ 3).
**ג. מסירת האזהרה בביקורת אם ידווח על קושי בנהיגה.** שגויה, האזהרה נועדה לתרופה העלולה להשפיע על נהיגה ואינה מותנית באירוע שכבר התרחש (עמ׳ 3).
**ד. מסירת האזהרה למשפחה כדי שתדריך את המטופל במקומה.** שגויה, החוזר דורש להזהיר את החולה; מסירת מידע למשפחה עשויה לסייע אך אינה תחליף לאזהרתו במקרה המתואר (עמ׳ 3).

מקור: משרד הבריאות, הבהרה מחדש של חובת הדיווח על נהגים, עמ׳ 3.

q: In which population did the PACIFIC trial evaluate durvalumab, according to Hazzard?
o: Resected early-stage disease before the start of adjuvant systemic therapy
Metastatic disease progressing after completion of a course of chemotherapy
Unresectable stage III disease controlled after concurrent chemotherapy and radiation
Resected stage III disease before the start of postoperative radiation therapy
explanation:
**PACIFIC** evaluated durvalumab in patients with unresectable stage III non-small-cell lung cancer whose disease was controlled after concurrent chemoradiation. The trial population is therefore defined by both disease stage and the treatment already completed, rather than by a postoperative treatment pathway. (p. 1426)
"In the PACIFIC trial, 713 patients with unresectable stage III NSCLC who had disease control after concurrent chemoradiation were randomized" (p. 1426)

**A. Resected early-stage disease before the start of adjuvant systemic therapy.** Wrong, the trial enrolled unresectable stage III disease after concurrent chemoradiation, not resected early-stage disease awaiting adjuvant therapy. (p. 1426)
**B. Metastatic disease progressing after completion of a course of chemotherapy.** Wrong, the trial population had controlled stage III disease, not metastatic disease progressing after chemotherapy. (p. 1426)
**C. Unresectable stage III disease controlled after concurrent chemotherapy and radiation.** Correct, this includes the unresectability, stage, disease control, and prior concurrent chemoradiation specified in the source. (p. 1426)
**D. Resected stage III disease before the start of postoperative radiation therapy.** Wrong, the trial enrolled unresectable disease after concurrent chemoradiation, not patients awaiting postoperative radiation. (p. 1426)

Source: Hazzard’s Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th ed., p. 1426.

q: גבר שוודי בן 75 מגיע לביקור בריאות שנתי. הוא הפסיק לעשן לפני 10 שנים לאחר היסטוריה של 40 שנות עישון, ושותה אלכוהול מדי פעם. הוא שואל על תוחלת החיים שלו בהשוואה לאשתו בת אותו הגיל. בהתבסס על מגמות אפידמיולוגיות עדכניות, מה המידע שאמור להנחות את הייעוץ?
o: פער תוחלת החיים בין המינים היה יציב על 7-8 שנים במשך עשורים
הפער גדל עקב אורח חיים בריא יותר של נשים
הפער מצטמצם מאז שנות ה-1980 ועומד כיום על כ-3.5 שנים
הפער משתנה באופן בלתי צפוי ולא ניתן להעריכו
explanation:
התשובה היא **פער שהצטמצם מאז שנות השמונים לכ־3.5 שנים**, לפי הנתונים ההיסטוריים המובאים בספר על שוודיה. נתון זה מתאר אוכלוסייה ואינו תחזית להפרש שנות החיים של בני הזוג המסוימים (עמ׳ 86).

**א. פער תוחלת החיים בין המינים היה יציב על 7-8 שנים במשך עשורים.** שגויה, הפער לא נשאר קבוע: הוא גדל אחרי מלחמת העולם השנייה, ולאחר מכן ירד. גם אופן הצגתו כשנים לעומת אחוז מתוחלת החיים משנה את התמונה (עמ׳ 85–86).
**ב. הפער גדל עקב אורח חיים בריא יותר של נשים.** שגויה, המקור מתאר צמצום, ולא התרחבות, של הפער בשוודיה מאז שנות השמונים (עמ׳ 86).
**ג. הפער מצטמצם מאז שנות ה-1980 ועומד כיום על כ-3.5 שנים.** נכונה, הפער בלידה ובגיל 50 גדל לאחר מלחמת העולם השנייה ואחר כך הצטמצם לכ־3.5 שנים. דפוס דומה תואר בארצות הברית, בקנדה, באוסטרליה, באיסלנד וברוב אירופה. השפעות מאוחרות של עישון, ובפרט ירידה מהירה יותר בתמותה הגברית הקשורה אליו, תורמות למגמה; היסטוריית הגמילה רלוונטית לייעוץ אך אינה מחליפה הערכה אישית (עמ׳ 86–87).
**ד. הפער משתנה באופן בלתי צפוי ולא ניתן להעריכו.** שגויה, יש דפוסי זמן מזוהים הניתנים לניתוח, גם אם קיימים הבדלים בין מדינות. אין מדובר בתנודות שאין אפשרות לתארן (עמ׳ 85–87).

מקור: Hazzard 8e, פרק 5, עמ׳ 85–87.

q: A 79-year-old man awaiting a below-knee amputation asks about returning to mobility with a prosthesis. Which functional assessment supports rehabilitation planning according to Hazzard?
o: Assess potential from arm strength and chronological age
Assess previous walking, medical status, and ability to learn
Assess potential from kidney disease stage and chronological age
Assess potential from diabetes duration and the prosthesis type
explanation:
**Post-amputation functional potential** depends on prior function, ability to meet the physiological demands of prosthetic use, and ability to learn new skills. Hazzard uses these considerations to develop rehabilitation goals rather than inferring potential from age or a single disease descriptor (p. 831). "Considerations in determining the potential functional status of someone after an amputation may include prior ability to walk," (p. 831).

**A. Assess potential from arm strength and chronological age.** Wrong, arm strength and age omit prior walking ability and the broader medical and learning assessment specified (p. 831).
**B. Assess previous walking, medical status, and ability to learn.** Correct, these are the three domains explicitly listed for estimating potential functional status (p. 831).
**C. Assess potential from kidney disease stage and chronological age.** Wrong, kidney disease belongs in medical assessment but does not replace prior walking ability or capacity to learn (p. 831).
**D. Assess potential from diabetes duration and the prosthesis type.** Wrong, disease duration and a device label do not supply the required assessment of function, medical demands, and learning (p. 831).

Source: Hazzard's Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th ed., pp. 831.

q: An 86-year-old man from assisted living presents with acute confusion and a positive CAM. At 3 a.m. he tried to leave for work. He has mild dementia, insomnia, and osteoarthritis. Six hours earlier he received tramadol 100 mg, trazodone 100 mg, and diphenhydramine 50 mg. Vital signs are normal. Which concern about oral diphenhydramine is specifically identified by the 2023 AGS Beers Criteria?
o: Its clearance increases with advancing age, reducing anticholinergic exposure.
Its anticholinergic effects carry a risk of confusion and delirium.
Its regular use as a hypnotic preserves responsiveness without tolerance.
Its use during delirium is favored because of protective cognitive effects.
explanation:
**Oral diphenhydramine** is listed among first-generation antihistamines to avoid because of substantial anticholinergic effects, reduced clearance with advanced age, and risk of confusion (p. 2057). Anticholinergics can induce or worsen **delirium**, so Beers recommends avoiding them in older adults with or at high risk of delirium (p. 2066).
"Highly anticholinergic; clearance reduced with advanced age, and tolerance develops when used as hypnotic; risk of confusion, dry mouth, constipation, and other anticholinergic effects or toxicity." (p. 2057).

**A. Its clearance increases with advancing age, reducing anticholinergic exposure.** Wrong, Beers describes reduced clearance with advanced age, not increased clearance; the proposed pharmacokinetic explanation conflicts with that description (p. 2057).
**B. Its anticholinergic effects carry a risk of confusion and delirium.** Correct, confusion is an explicit anticholinergic risk, and anticholinergics can induce or worsen delirium; these are relevant medication concerns in this presentation (pp. 2057, 2066).
**C. Its regular use as a hypnotic preserves responsiveness without tolerance.** Wrong, Beers states that tolerance develops when these antihistamines are used as hypnotics, so sustained responsiveness without tolerance is not the stated rationale (p. 2057).
**D. Its use during delirium is favored because of protective cognitive effects.** Wrong, the recommendation is to avoid anticholinergics in patients with delirium because they can induce or worsen it, rather than use them for cognitive protection (p. 2066).

Source: AGS Beers Criteria, 2023, pp. 2057, 2066.

q: An older woman takes warfarin together with an SSRI. If the combination is needed, which risk and monitoring recommendation matches Beers 2023?
o: Reduced bleeding risk and less frequent INR monitoring
Increased bleeding risk and close INR monitoring
Reduced bleeding risk and close INR monitoring
Increased bleeding risk and less frequent INR monitoring
explanation:
**Warfarin–SSRI coadministration increases bleeding risk**. Beers recommends avoiding the combination when possible and close INR monitoring when it is used, rather than relaxing surveillance (p. 2071). "Avoid when possible; if used together, monitor INR closely." (p. 2071)

**A. Reduced bleeding risk and less frequent INR monitoring.** Wrong, the table identifies increased bleeding risk and calls for close monitoring; reduced risk does not justify less surveillance (p. 2071).
**B. Increased bleeding risk and close INR monitoring.** Correct, this pairs the stated bleeding risk with the specified monitoring response when coadministration is necessary (p. 2071).
**C. Reduced bleeding risk and close INR monitoring.** Wrong, close monitoring matches the recommendation, but the proposed reduced bleeding risk does not match its rationale (p. 2071).
**D. Increased bleeding risk and less frequent INR monitoring.** Wrong, the risk is correctly identified, but less frequent monitoring is inconsistent with the close monitoring recommended for this combination (p. 2071).

Source: AGS Beers Criteria 2023, pp. 2071.
ref: Hazzard Ch 22 — MEDICATION PRESCRIBING AND DE-PRESCRIBING

q: באיזה מהבאים מתוארת תופעת לוואי המתאימה לתרופה האנטי-פסיכוטיות הרשומה?
o: QUETIAPINE (SEROQUEL) גורם לעוררות
OLANZEPINE (ZYPREXA) גורם לירידה במשקל
CLOZAPINE ( LEPONEX) גורם לנויטרופניה
HALOPERIDOL (HALIDOL) גורם לבחילות
explanation:
**Clozapine** is associated with neutropenia and agranulocytosis, requiring blood monitoring. Table 60-8 specifies weekly blood draws during the first six months; no later monitoring schedule is established here (p. 928).

**A. Quetiapine (Seroquel) causes arousal.** Wrong, sedation is the characteristic effect listed for quetiapine, so arousal is not the expected pairing (p. 928).
**B. Olanzapine (Zyprexa) causes weight loss.** Wrong, the table assigns olanzapine a high risk of weight gain, not the proposed direction of change (p. 928).
**C. Clozapine (Leponex) causes neutropenia.** Correct, the text identifies neutropenia as a serious adverse effect, and the table also lists agranulocytosis and blood monitoring (p. 928).
**D. Haloperidol (Halidol) causes nausea.** Wrong, Hazzard emphasizes its high extrapyramidal risk and also includes haloperidol among antiemetic treatments; nausea is not the characteristic pairing sought (pp. 928, 1391).

Source: Hazzard 8e, pp. 928, 1391.
referenceNote: Printed IMA citation retained; checked explanation source: Hazzard 8e · p. 928,946-947.

q: An immobilized older patient wears heel protectors. Why do these not remove the need to consider heel offloading?
o: They reduce heel pressure while increasing friction between the heel and the bed.
They reduce heel pressure and friction, making elevation a redundant measure.
They increase heel pressure and friction, making them unsuitable for skin protection.
They reduce heel friction while leaving the need for pressure relief unaddressed.
explanation:
**Friction protection and pressure relief** are distinct parts of preventing heel injury (p. 685). The chapter warns: “Even though heel, ankle, and elbow protectors do nothing to reduce or relieve pressure, they can be effective aids against friction.” (p. 685). Heel elevation is separately described as useful prevention.

**A. They reduce heel pressure while increasing friction between the heel and the bed.** Wrong, the source describes friction protection without pressure relief (p. 685).
**B. They reduce heel pressure and friction, making elevation a redundant measure.** Wrong, protectors do not relieve pressure; lifting the heel off the bed is a separate preventive measure (p. 685).
**C. They increase heel pressure and friction, making them unsuitable for skin protection.** Wrong, the source calls these effective aids against friction, not causes of increased friction (p. 685).
**D. They reduce heel friction while leaving the need for pressure relief unaddressed.** Correct, protection from rubbing does not provide the pressure relief achieved by lifting the heel off the bed (p. 685).

Source: Hazzard’s Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8e, pp. 685.

q: Which FDA-approved drug extends survival and delays the need for ventilation in ALS?
o: Riluzole
Cholinesterase inhibitors
Anticholinergic medications
Levodopa
explanation:
**Riluzole** is distinguished here by an effect on ALS survival and ventilatory support, rather than symptom relief alone. The chapter states that it “extends survival and delays the need for ventilation support,” while describing other care as directed at symptoms and quality of life (p. 991).

**A. Riluzole.** Correct, this is the agent specifically credited with both survival extension and delayed ventilation in ALS (p. 991).
**B. Cholinesterase inhibitors.** Wrong, the ALS treatment passage does not attribute either endpoint to this class; it cannot substitute for the agent with the stated disease-course benefit (p. 991).
**C. Anticholinergic medications.** Wrong, this class is not identified as prolonging survival or delaying ventilation in the ALS passage, so symptom-directed drug use would not establish the benefit asked about (p. 991).
**D. Levodopa.** Wrong, this drug is not credited with the specified ALS outcomes in the chapter; the named survival-prolonging agent is riluzole (p. 991).

Source: Hazzard’s Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8e, pp. 991.

q: An older adult taking an NSAID becomes volume depleted. Which assessment principle follows Hazzard’s discussion of acute kidney injury?
o: Use the absence of renal symptoms as strong evidence against AKI
Treat medication toxicity as less relevant to AKI with increasing age
Focus drug-related risk on contrast rather than common oral medications
Assess volume depletion and medication toxicity as contributors to AKI
explanation:
**Older-adult AKI risk** reflects both physiologic stress and medication exposure. The chapter states, "Polypharmacy and drug toxicity exacerbate the susceptibility of older adults to AKI." It also identifies hypovolemia as an important risk. Because AKI can be asymptomatic and detected by a creatinine rise, assessment should not depend on overt symptoms (p. 1282).

**A. Use the absence of renal symptoms as strong evidence against AKI.** Wrong, the source explicitly allows asymptomatic AKI detected by elevated creatinine, so absence of symptoms cannot rule it out (p. 1282).
**B. Treat medication toxicity as less relevant to AKI with increasing age.** Wrong, the chapter says drug toxicity exacerbates older adults’ susceptibility rather than becoming less relevant with age (p. 1282).
**C. Focus drug-related risk on contrast rather than common oral medications.** Wrong, NSAIDs, diuretics, ACE inhibitors, ARBs and antibiotics are explicitly listed alongside the separate discussion of contrast; focusing only on contrast misses common drug exposures (p. 1282).
**D. Assess volume depletion and medication toxicity as contributors to AKI.** Correct, this considers both contributors identified on the page and applies them to the patient’s volume depletion and NSAID exposure (p. 1282).

Source: Hazzard’s Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th ed., p. 1282.

q: Is oxaliplatin's adjuvant survival benefit established equally in all older adults?
o: Yes - the MOSAIC older subgroup gained survival from adding oxaliplatin
No - several older-subgroup analyses show no added survival benefit
Yes - the updated ACCENT analysis established survival benefit in older subgroups
No - the chapter reserves oxaliplatin for adults with substantial comorbidity
explanation:
Older-subgroup evidence on adjuvant oxaliplatin is mixed; several analyses show no added survival benefit, and it can be considered for fit adults with minimal comorbidity (p1441).

A. Yes - the MOSAIC older subgroup gained survival from adding oxaliplatin: ACCENT, MOSAIC older-subgroup and NSABP C-07 findings do not establish this uniform benefit (p1441).
D. No - the chapter reserves oxaliplatin for adults with substantial comorbidity: The text allows consideration for fit adults with minimal comorbidities (p1441).
C. Yes - the updated ACCENT analysis established survival benefit in older subgroups: The updated ACCENT analysis showed no DFS or OS benefit among older adults (p1441).
